runConfig.positivePrompt: Scientific educational image-to-video for ages five to fourteen. Static locked wide camera, one continuous forward-only five-second shot with no cuts. Preserve the attached approved still as the exact first-frame identity, anatomy, left-facing full-body composition, lighting, palette, skin markings, terrain, vegetation, and crop reference. Exactly one complete Giganotosaurus carolinii remains in frame with one long low rectangular skull, narrow snout, low lacrimal ridge, two short three-fingered forelimbs, exactly two planted hind limbs, and one complete continuous tail. After a brief closed-mouth hold, the dinosaur itself performs one restrained silent display in a single temporal direction: the complete head and connected muscular neck rise only four degrees while only the lower jaw opens smoothly at the natural hinge to a moderate eighteen-to-twenty-two-degree gape. The throat expands once and the final second holds the open-mouth pose. Keep the upper skull, snout length, lacrimal ridge, eye, nostril, stable attached tooth rows, low tongue, and neck thickness consistent. Keep the torso, pelvis, arms, both feet, every readable toe, and full tail planted and unchanged. Keep every background element completely still. The jaw never closes and the head never returns; no reverse, recoil, repeated roar, walk, or loop.
